The first launch failed.

We tried a waitlist, and nobody signed up.

We tried paid ads, and the clicks cost more than the customers were worth.

We tried cold email, and three people replied. One of them became our first real customer: a dentist in Leeds who kept losing patients to missed appointments.

That said, the dentist taught us more than the ads did. She didn't want software — she wanted fewer empty chairs on Monday mornings. It wasn't a marketing problem. It was a product problem. We rebuilt the reminder flow around her week: the night-before text, the morning-of call, the empty-slot alert. Her referrals brought us the next ten customers — all of them dentists.
